references.text: Balak builds seven altars and offers a bull and a ram on each altar, the same pattern repeated here at the top of Pisgah.
Balak takes Balaam to a third place (Peor) and again builds seven altars with the same sacrificial ritual.
Balak leads Balaam to Bamoth-Baal, the first high place from which to see the people of Israel, leading to the series of viewing points.
Moses goes up to the top of Pisgah to see the land, the same geographical location mentioned in this text.
Moses goes up the mountain of Pisgah from the plains of Moab, the same summit that Balak led Balaam to.
Pisgah is mentioned as a geographical landmark in Israel's journey, the same mountain that Balaam was brought to.
